audit.whatIsWrong: The ENTIRE content layer is written for pre-rework Aurelion Sol. It refers to 'your unscaled early stars', 'your stars are still orbiting wide', 'stacked star orbit', 'max Starsurge range', 'your comet clear', 'a full E stun', and 'Voidlink (E)'. Affected fields: whys[0], whys[1], whys[3], whys[5], whys[6], spikes[0], spikes[2], spikes[3], early, late, wants.you[0], wants.you[1], wants.you[2].
audit.why: Current Aurelion Sol has Breath of Light (Q, a 750 channel), Astral Flight (W), a black hole (E, 750, pull plus execute) and Falling Star / The Skies Descend (R, 1250 stun). There is no orbit, no Starsurge, no comet, no E stun, and 'Voidlink' is not an ability any champion has. Every piece of positional advice on this page therefore told the reader to play around mechanics that do not exist.
audit.corrected: All thirteen fields rewritten to the real kit — 750 channel, 12s black hole, 22s Astral Flight, 1250 Falling Star, permanent stardust.
sources: ownerKit ability list and text in the brief

audit.whatIsWrong: Vanguard's Edge is described as 'dashes to you, stuns, and shreds your resistances' in content mid, and 'dashes, stuns, and shreds resistances' in spikes[1].
audit.why: It does none of those three. enemyKit R: 'Irelia fires a massive number of blades that explode outward upon hitting an enemy champion. Enemies hit by the blades are damaged and Marked. Afterwards the blades form a wall that will damage and slow enemies that walk through it.' It is a 950-range projectile that Marks and builds a wall. The wall is the actual danger to Aurelion Sol precisely because he has no dash — which is the missingInteractions terrain-cuts-retreat rule, and here that flag is CORRECT (the wall is in Riot's own text).
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text, mid, whys[4] and wants.foe[1] rewritten around Mark plus wall plus slow at 950, on a 125s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive facts were nowhere on the page: Flawless Duet GROUNDS as well as stuns, and Bladesurge's cooldown REFRESHES on a Marked target or a target that dies to it.
audit.why: enemyKit E carries the grounding flag with hardCC — Astral Flight is a movement ability, so a landed Duet removes Aurelion Sol's only escape rather than merely interrupting him. And enemyKit Q: 'If the target is Marked or dies to Bladesurge, its cooldown refreshes' — which is why a wave of minions is an infinite dash and why the E-then-Q order is the whole combo. The page called E 'her stun setup' and left it there.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, enemyWin, tradeGood, tradeBad, dontsFull[1].d, dontsFull[2].d, whys[1], whys[2], whys[3], spikes[0].text, early and wants.foe[0] now state both.

audit.whatIsWrong: The needs-antiheal rule was absent from lane advice — only report[8] mentioned anti-heal in passing, and it said 'his sustain'.
audit.why: Bladesurge heals Irelia on every dash and refreshes off Marks and minion kills, so chip damage without Grievous Wounds funds her rather than hurting her.
audit.corrected: ahead, breakdown.feeding, wants.you[1] and content late now make Grievous Wounds a condition on fighting her.

The last two rows go to Aurelion Sol on range and scaling — Falling Star reaches 1250 against a 950 Vanguard's Edge, and the full layer's own whys for rows 5 and 6 already describe Aurelion Sol winning. notes: This page had the single largest defect in my slice: the ENTIRE content layer was written for pre-rework Aurelion Sol. Thirteen fields referenced 'orbiting stars', 'Starsurge', 'comet clear', 'a full E stun' and 'Voidlink (E)' — none of which exist in the current kit, and 'Voidlink' is not an ability on any champion. A reader following wants.you[2] would be waiting for a disengage button they do not have. Worth checking whether other Aurelion Sol matchups share this content block; if the old-kit text was templated across the champion, this will not be the only page. Second-largest: Vanguard's Edge was described as a dash + stun + resistance shred in two places when Riot's text says it fires blades that Mark and then form a damaging, slowing WALL — which matters more, not less, because Aurelion Sol has no dash to cross it. Unlike galio, the terrain flag on Irelia's R is genuine and I used it. Difficulty left at HARD 8/10 (49.27%), consistent with how I treated ekko and fizz.
